tasks.prompt: Trace subscription-backed Scout process execution from configuration through JSON stream handling and process-tree cleanup. Cite the direct implementation and checks.
Trace how repository tool definitions reach a model request and how returned calls are sandboxed, executed, and turned into validated citations. Cite budget and timeout paths.
Trace one chat completion request through route selection, provider fallback, and final HTTP error mapping. Cite the direct implementation paths.

result_layout: Sanitized aggregates are in summary.json. Raw commands, streams, retries, and provider metadata remain under private/.
methodology: Two repeats per arm in deterministic randomized order. Three concurrent Go workers invoked the production Gigo gateway through a local credential-hiding model-name adapter. Both arms used identical prompts and bounded Scout settings; the treatment enabled the candidate Scout binary and CodeGraph configuration. Separate five-repeat process fixtures measured timeout behavior, and the existing 111-run routing matrix measured route quality.

protocol.order_policy: Deterministic shuffle with PCG seed (20260827, 1); three concurrent workers.
protocol.network_policy: Production Gigo endpoint; no credentials written to artifacts.
protocol.cache_policy: Shared compiled binaries; immutable per-attempt result directories; no model response cache.

limitations: Neither benchmark repository had a .codegraph index at execution time, so the treatment could not exercise CodeGraph and this run cannot support a tool-impact claim.
The free OpenRouter model produced no useful final answers and hit three rate-limit or upstream failures in the first complete matrix.
The authenticated model catalog advertised Gemini tool support incorrectly for the adapter, and the preferred paid OpenRouter route had no credits; those failed retries are retained under private/.
Repository-task quality and citation recall are too low for headline use. The process-timeout result is independent and conclusive.
